official.deadline_note: Rotary publishes one central deadline for all applicants worldwide and no separate institutional deadlines; the online application is available 1 February - 15 May every year, and the 2028-29 round opens 1 February 2027.
official.status_note: "The 2027-28 Rotary Peace Fellowship application is now closed. The 2028-29 Rotary Peace Fellowship application will be available online in February 2027."
official.tuition_coverage_note: "The fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses." The master's program postcard adds health insurance to what the fellowship pays for.
benefits: Full funding for a master's degree or postgraduate certificate at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers
Up to 50 fellowships for master's degrees and up to 120 for certificate studies awarded each year (up to 170 total)
Master's fellowships also pay for health insurance per Rotary's program postcard
Access to a global network of more than 1,900 Rotary Peace Fellows working in over 140 countries since 2002
Master's programme includes a self-designed two- to three-month applied field experience; certificate programme includes field studies and a nine-month social change initiative
eligibility: At least three years of full-time relevant experience in peace or development work for the master's program (five years for the Duke program); at least five years for the certificate program
Bachelor's degree and demonstrated leadership skills, with a strong and proven commitment to cross-cultural understanding and peace

Master's candidates must have at least three years between completing their most recent academic degree and the intended fellowship start date; anyone currently enrolled, or enrolling in the upcoming academic year, is not eligible
Active Rotary members, Rotaract members who are also Rotary members, and their spouses or lineal descendants are not eligible; Rotaract members who are not also Rotary club members are eligible
Certificate candidates must be from a certificate center region (Africa, Middle East, Asia) or have strong ties or interest in working with communities from those regions
Rotary Peace Fellows who completed the certificate program and Global Grant Scholarship recipients must wait three years between that program's end date and the intended fellowship start date
requirements: Submit the online application to The Rotary Foundation during the 1 February - 15 May window
Be proficient in English; master's candidates whose first language is not English must provide English language standardized test scores
Demonstrate relevant professional experience in peacebuilding and/or community or international development, plus potential for future growth and impact
Certificate candidates must propose a feasible Social Change Initiative aligned with Rotary's mission
selection_criteria: Personal, academic, and professional achievements, assessed in a globally competitive process
Applications are screened for eligibility; qualified applications move forward for further review and evaluation
Selected candidates are notified in November
coverage: Health insurance (listed for the master's fellowship)
application_method: Visit rotary.org/peace-fellowships and research the curriculum at each Rotary Peace Center during the off-season
Submit the online application through The Rotary Foundation's Peace Fellowship application portal once it opens on 1 February
Upload the resume, recommendations, video statement and essays, transcripts (master's), English test scores (master's), and social impact plan (certificate)
Engage a local or online Rotary club for mentorship; a club or district recommendation is optional but encouraged and does not require district funding support
Submit by 15 May - all applications are considered final upon submission
official.application_route: Apply online through The Rotary Foundation's Peace Fellowship application portal during the 1 February - 15 May window each year.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to candidates from all backgrounds and countries; however, master's fellowship recipients may not study at a Rotary Peace Center in their home countries, and certificate candidates must be from, or have strong ties or interest in, a certificate center region (Africa, Middle East, Asia).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - The Rotary Foundation welcomes eligible candidates from all backgrounds, and fellows study at centers outside their home countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Peace and development studies. Certificate applicants must align with a center region: Makerere University (Africa), Bahcesehir University (Middle East/North Africa), or Symbiosis International University (Asia).
official.research_requirement: Master's fellows complete a self-designed two- to three-month applied field experience and present their master's research at a final seminar; certificate fellows must propose a feasible Social Change Initiative aligned with Rotary's mission.
official.duration: Master's degree: 15 to 24 months including a two- to three-month field study. Certificate: one-year blended learning program (two-week online preliminary course, ten weeks on-site, nine-month social change initiative, one-week capstone seminar).
official.description: Rotary awards up to 170 funded fellowships a year for dedicated leaders from around the world to study at one of eight peace centers, developing the capacity of peace and development professionals to become effective catalysts for peace. The fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses, and support either a master's degree or a one-year professional development certificate.
official.region: Global (Rotary Peace Centers in the USA, Japan, England, Australia, Sweden, Uganda, Turkiye, and India)
official.program_type: Fully funded postgraduate fellowship: master's degree or professional development certificate in peace and development
official.english_requirement: Candidates must be proficient in English; master's candidates whose first language is not English must provide English language standardized test scores.

not_confirmed: funding_amount - Rotary publishes no monetary value for the fellowship on any official page or program document
study_mode - full-time/part-time wording is not published for either program
verification.notes: Coverage list, eligibility rules, required documents, the 1 February - 15 May window, and current-cycle status were confirmed on rotary.org program pages plus Rotary's own application announcement PDF, program overview presentation, master's postcard, and relevant-experience guide; no dollar figure is published anywhere on the awarding body's domain.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the few fully funded peace and development fellowships that pays tuition, room and board, round-trip travel, and field-study costs without asking you to secure a Rotary sponsor's money. You choose between a 15-24 month master's at five partner universities (USA, Japan, UK, Australia, Sweden) and a one-year certificate at Makerere, Bahcesehir, or Symbiosis, and the route differs mainly by career stage: three years of relevant experience for the master's track versus five for the certificate. The window is short and unforgiving once you are inside it - everything must be in the portal by 15 May, applications are final on submission, and winners hear only in November, so plan your other offers around that lag. Note that master's fellows cannot study in their home country, which shapes your center choice from day one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career peacebuilding and development professionals with a bachelor's degree and 3-5 years of directly relevant work who want a funded degree or certificate outside their home country.
application_readiness_checklist: Map your work history against Rotary's ten relevant-experience categories and collect dates and titles that prove full-time peace or development work, since administrative, retail, and purely technical roles generally do not count
Line up academic or professional referees months ahead - the portal needs recommendations alongside your resume, video statement, and essays
For the master's track, book your English proficiency test early and confirm the scores your preferred university requires, and request transcripts well before February
For the certificate track, draft the feasible Social Change Initiative tied to your center region (Africa, Middle East/North Africa, or Asia) before the window opens
Use the Club Finder to engage a Rotary or Rotaract club for mentorship and an optional club or district recommendation, which carries no funding obligation
Write every statement yourself - Rotary disqualifies applications containing AI-generated content, so draft early and keep an originality trail
common_rejection_risks: Work experience that is only adjacent to peacebuilding: Rotary generally excludes office management, customer service, HR, retail, restaurant, and security roles, and treats engineering, IT, and fund-development roles as relevant only with a direct development outcome
Applying while enrolled in any degree program, or within three years of finishing your most recent degree for the master's track
AI-generated or non-original application content, which disqualifies the application outright
Missing English test scores as a master's candidate whose first language is not English, or missing transcripts
Choosing a certificate center whose region you cannot credibly connect to, or a master's center located in your home country
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Rotary's published coverage stops at tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, internship and field-study expenses, and health insurance; personal spending, visa fees, and costs for accompanying family members are not listed as covered, and no stipend figure is published to budget against.
document_audit: Transcripts are a master's-only requirement - certificate applicants submit a social impact plan instead, so do not mix the two checklists
English test scores are required for master's candidates whose first language is not English, and each partner university sets its own score expectations
The video statement, essays, and recommendations are all part of one submission; a late referee effectively means a missed cycle because the portal finalizes at 15 May
Keep an unedited record of your own drafting to defend against the AI-content rule if queried
alerts: The 2027-28 cycle is already closed - the next application opens on 1 February 2027 and shuts on 15 May 2027, giving roughly a 15-week window
Notification lands in November, months after submission, so keep fallback study or work options alive through the autumn
Applications are considered final on submission, so there is no editing after 15 May
Active Rotary or dual Rotaract-Rotary members, and their spouses and lineal descendants, are barred - non-dual Rotaract members remain eligible
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete one online application in The Rotary Foundation's portal during the 1 February - 15 May window with resume, recommendations, video statement, essays, transcripts and English scores (master's) or social impact plan (certificate); it is screened for eligibility, reviewed by Rotary Peace Centers staff, and outcomes arrive in November.
